svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "Interphase (not part of mitosis): the cell grows, DNA replicates so each chromosome becomes two sister chromatids, and the centrosome duplicates. The chromosomes are long and thin (chromatin), so they are not visible."], [3, "Prophase: the chromosomes condense (supercoil), becoming short and thick, each with two sister chromatids joined at a centromere. The nucleolus disappears, the centrosomes move to opposite poles and the spindle forms. At the end the nuclear envelope breaks down."], [6, "Metaphase: the chromosomes line up one by one on the equator of the spindle. Spindle fibres from both poles attach to the centromere of each chromosome."], [9, "Anaphase: the centromeres divide and the spindle fibres shorten, pulling the sister chromatids to opposite poles, centromere first. Each pole receives one copy of every chromosome."], [12, "Telophase: the chromatids (now called chromosomes) reach the poles and uncoil. A nuclear envelope and nucleolus form around each set, and the spindle breaks down."], [15, "Cytokinesis: the cell surface membrane pinches inwards (a cleavage furrow) and divides the cytoplasm. Two daughter cells form, genetically identical to each other and to the parent cell (2n = 4)."]]
svg.title: Mitosis in an animal cell
svg.desc: An animated animal cell with two pairs of homologous chromosomes going through interphase, prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase and cytokinesis.
svg.text: Red chromosomes came from the mother, blue from the father. Press Play, or step through the stages.

g.data-info: In an animal cell the membrane pinches in at the end (cleavage furrow) to divide the cytoplasm: cytokinesis.
The middle of the spindle, where the chromosomes line up in metaphase.
Breaks down at the end of prophase so the spindle can reach the chromosomes; re-forms around each set of chromosomes in telophase.
Disappears in prophase and re-forms in telophase.
Duplicate in interphase and move to opposite poles in prophase, where they organise the spindle.
Microtubules from each pole that attach to the centromeres and, by shortening, pull the sister chromatids apart.
Each chromosome was copied in interphase, so in prophase and metaphase it is two identical sister chromatids joined at a centromere. Red: from the mother; blue: from the father.

svg.text: Not to scale. Mitosis gives two cells with the same number and type of chromosomes as the parent: growth, repair and asexual reproduction.
